children: U.S. soybean, wheat and corn futures rose on Wednesday, recovering from earlier losses triggered by falling crude oil prices.
on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was up 0.28% at $13.22-1/2 a bushel, as of 0503 GMT, marking the third consecutive sessions of gains.
added 0.62% to $7.33 a bushel and corn

Soybean prices remained supported by a monthly industry report showing that August soybean crushing was lower than expected, as well as a rise in Chinese demand for U.S. supplies ahead of Chinese President Xi Jinping's expected visit to Washington later this month.

Concerns over harvest delays also lent support to soybean and corn prices. Harvesting was under way across the U.S. Midwest, although heavy rain delayed fieldwork in parts of Iowa, the nation's largest corn producer and second-largest soybean producer.

In South America, Brazilian crop agency Conab forecast the country's 2026/27 soybean production at 181.64 million metric tons, up 0.7% from the previous year but below the U.S. Department of Agriculture's current forecast of 186 million metric tons.
Wheat prices gained as hopes for a military de-escalation in the Black Sea grain-export region faded following further attacks on infrastructure.
Meanwhile, Algeria's state grains agency OAIC bought about 500,000 metric tons of milling wheat in an international tender that closed on Tuesday, European traders said.
Ahead of a Statistics Canada crop report due on Wednesday, analysts surveyed by Reuters, on average, expected the agency to estimate Canada's 2026 all-wheat harvest at 36.73 million metric tons.
Commodity funds were net buyers of CBOT corn, soy and wheat futures, traders said on Tuesday. (CBOT/FUNDS)
